heroHeadline: EU FAC DEFENCE CONVENES — KALLAS: EUROPE MUST DEFINE ITS OWN RED LINES ON RUSSIA; €63B UKRAINE AID REVIEWED; €90B DEFENSE LOAN DEBATED; DUAL EMERGENCY TRACK WITH NATO HELSINGBORG PREP UNDERWAY
heroSubtitle: On May 12, 2026, EU defence and foreign ministers met in Brussels for the EU Foreign Affairs Council (Defence) — the EU institutional counterpart to NATO's Helsingborg emergency pre-briefing track. Chaired by EU High Representative Kaja Kallas, with NATO Deputy Secretary General Radmila Shekerinska and Ukrainian Defence Minister Mykhailo Fedorov (VTC) participating, the session reviewed the updated EU Threat Analysis, EU total military support for Ukraine (€63B since 2022, €25B in 2025 alone), and debated a proposed €90B EU defense loan (€60B defense-targeted). Kallas defined Europe's shift from dependency to autonomy: 'For Europe to take a more active role, we must agree amongst ourselves what we want to talk to Russia about and what our red lines are.' Hungary's blocking of €6.6B in European Peace Facility funds left €43B in member-state reimbursements unresolved. Background: May 11 — Rutte meets Ukrainian FM Sybiha at NATO HQ; Helsingborg (May 21–22) configured as emergency session with four agenda clusters; Norway surpasses US in per-capita defense spending; Poland pushes 5% by 2030. May 10 — formal allied contingency planning. May 9 — Rasmussen 'disintegrating'; Italy/Spain drawdowns forecast. May 8 — 'Something fundamental has broken' (Daalder). May 7 — 'terror incubators' CT strategy. May 5 — Tomahawk cancelled. May 1 — 5,000 from Germany. Next: Helsingborg FMM May 21–22 (first NATO ministerial on Swedish soil); Ankara Leaders' Summit July 7–8.
